findings.title: A crashed renderer anywhere in the session (no dialog at all) locks the WHOLE CLI session: every gated command exits 3 claiming "a unknown dialog is open", dialog accept/dismiss refuses, tabs/closetab/nav are gated, only sutradhar close (destroying every tab and non-profile state) escapes. Regression vs the pre-FR2-04 CLI, which recovers in one command.

reproduction.rate: PURE CLI (nav -> newtab -> nav chrome://crash -> snap/tabs/dialog/dialog accept/nav/snap): cur 2/2 permanent lockout (tabs=3 nav=3 snap=3, dialog accept=1), pre-FR2-04 master dist 2/2 recovered (tabs=0 nav=0 snap=0). Observer Page.crash variant: cur 4/4 (bg + active tab) lockout vs master 0/4. a6 N5 4/4, signal-attack 2/2 (crashed) + 2/2 (chrome://hang).

findings.mechanism: The warden proactively confirms the tab (confirmedResponsiveSince) while healthy. After the crash, Performance.getMetrics times out, so listWithLiveness reports it as an unknown entry with confirmedSafe=true. runDialogGate blocks on ANY hint entry (allHint -> blockWith), selectDialog skips confirmedSafe entries (dialog accept -> "no dialog is open to accept", exit 1), tryRecoverUnknownTarget refuses confirmedSafe, and tabs/closetab/nav/reload are not exempt verbs. A crashed renderer never recovers on its own, so unlike the GAP-240 sync-XHR false block (accepted because it is transient) this block is permanent.
findings.whyNotAlreadyAccepted: audit-3 listed crashed/hung renderers under GAP-240 and fix-3/escalation-1 accepted the false BLOCK on the premise that a busy page blocks one command transiently and recovery must not close a healthy tab; audit-4/5 re-ran the crash case and only checked that recovery refused to close it. Nobody checked the escape path or compared with master: for a crash the block is permanent and the refused recovery is exactly what removes every in-session escape.
findings.specConflict: spec 2.8.2 step 1: a blocked target with no dialog known counts as busy and the gate proceeds with a Note; R1/D-4: exit 3 means blocked by an open dialog. Here there is provably no dialog (the tool itself says its history proves it), yet the tool reports one and exits 3 forever.
findings.fixDirection: Small, not architectural: exclude crashed targets (Target.targetCrashed / Inspector.targetCrashed) from the gate, and give every blocking state an in-session escape that does not need runtime.attach (e.g. tabs/closetab served from browser-level Target.getTargets + Target.closeTarget, or an explicit dialog close <targetId>).

findings.severity: major harm class (same as audit-5 GAP-252), narrower reach
findings.title: GAP-252 fix is incomplete: its anchor is the opener, so when the opener window is gone (e.g. a script-opened compose/search window that closes itself after opening popups) the two cross-site sibling popups are unlinked again and dialog accept closes the INNOCENT older popup first

reproduction.rate: raw-CDP N3-type252-openerclosed-g0: 5/8 innocent closed first (1/2 + 4/6); pure CLI (opener window closes itself): 2/5; with the opener still alive: 0 wrong closes (escalation-2 fix holds)

findings.mechanism: attributeDialogHolders links siblings only through a KNOWN opener (allKnown); a closed opener is no longer in browser.targets(), so each never-confirmed sibling is its own root and its own holder; selectDialog then picks FIFO by synthesized openedAt (targets() order), i.e. the older innocent. The innocent is never-confirmed because it was born into the renderer the holder blocked within milliseconds (same root as the disclosed residual: never-confirmed is treated as candidate).

residualJudgement.q1_narrowness: Reproduced and measured. Pure CLI: a popup/new tab whose own load does a sync XHR still outstanding ~6s after creation is closed by the recommended dialog accept 15/15 (same-site button popup 6/6, target=_blank link 3/3, cross-site popup 3/3, plus 3/3 for an opener that does a sync XHR right after window.open("") = GAP-251 at gap 0, which the escalation-2 binding decision explicitly required to be pinned no-close); a 3s XHR finishes before accept and survives 6/6 (it even loads). Heavy parse/layout and JS busy loops did not produce a close. Real-web frequency: sync XHR is deprecated but still common in legacy apps (jQuery async:false); it only matters with a multi-second endpoint and an agent that follows the hint. Rare, but WIDER than disclosed (not only the popup own first script: also the opener blocking right after window.open and plain target=_blank links).
residualJudgement.q2_signal: None found. discriminator-probe.mjs compared blocked-from-birth-by-dialog vs by-sync-XHR for both about:blank and URL popups, 2 trials each, across Target.getTargetInfo (url/title/attached/canAccessOpener/openerFrameId), Page.getNavigationHistory, Page.handleJavaScriptDialog (fresh session: No dialog is showing in both), Page.captureScreenshot, Performance.getMetrics, Runtime.evaluate, DOM.getDocument, Page.getFrameTree, Memory.getDOMCounters, Page.getLayoutMetrics, Network.enable, Page.enable, and renderer CPU time (SystemInfo.getProcessInfo): identical in every pair (browser-side answers identical, renderer-side all time out, CPU idle). The only discriminator is history: whether a Page-enabled listener existed before the first script ran. That is achievable structurally for URL-navigating popups (a warden-owned Target.setAutoAttach({waitForDebuggerOnStart:true}) so Page.enable precedes the popup first script), not for the about:blank synchronous-from-opener shape.
residualJudgement.q3_harm: Closing loses the popup and its in-flight work (the 3s variants show it would have loaded normally); in the same-renderer case it does not even unblock the opener (still blocked afterwards 4/4). It is not silent (the message names the tab, often with URL) and only happens on an explicit dialog accept|dismiss, never under --dialog policies. The alternative (refuse) turns every real load-time-alert popup -- which the warden consistently misses (reactive-*-inline, link-deadend) -- back into GAP-246 dead ends that only close escapes. Verdict on the residual alone: ACCEPTABLE to ship as a disclosed limitation (it would not by itself fail this audit), provided the docs state it and the disclosure is widened to the shapes above.

blockedDiagnosis.rootCause: Every FR2-04 cycle since fix-1 has patched one edge of the same inference: the design infers dialog state from a renderer-liveness probe that can only say answering or not answering, then layers heuristics (opener topology, newest-leaf, confirmedResponsiveSince history, known-opener anchors) on top of it to decide two different things at once: whether to block every command, and which tab it is safe to close. A6-01 is the block half failing (a provably non-dialog, never-recovering target blocks everything, with no escape because the escape verbs are gated too). A6-02 and the residual are the close half failing (never-confirmed is treated as candidate, and any missing anchor turns FIFO order into the decision).
whatMustChange: 1. Block only on positive evidence or a real attach hazard, never on unconfirmed inference alone: crashed targets excluded outright (Target.targetCrashed / Inspector.targetCrashed), and confirmed-safe busy targets reported as busy (spec 2.8.2 step 1), with attach made safe against them (lazy page adoption / bounded page init) instead of gating every verb.

2. Always keep an in-session escape that does not call runtime.attach: tabs and closetab served from browser-level Target.getTargets / Target.closeTarget, so no blocking state can require sutradhar close.

3. Make untracked dialogs structurally impossible for navigating popups: the warden holds its own browser-level Target.setAutoAttach({autoAttach:true, waitForDebuggerOnStart:true, flatten:true}) and sends Page.enable before Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger, so a URL popup is Page-enabled before its first script. Then blocked + untracked means busy for those popups and recovery never has to guess. Only the about:blank popup driven synchronously by its opener stays ambiguous.

4. Replace implicit recovery (dialog accept closes a guessed holder chosen FIFO among candidates) with explicit targeting: list the candidate tabs with ids and URLs and require dialog close <targetId>. The tool never picks among several unconfirmed candidates.
blockedDiagnosis.smallestPatchThatWouldHaveClosedA6_01: exclude crashed targets and ungate closetab/tabs via browser-level CDP; this is a small patch, but no fix cycles remain.
